Triggers.value: Undergoing a medical examination or procedure

Threat.value: Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame
My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger
Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience

Memory.value: When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened.
When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

Negative Appraisals.value: My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe
My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy
I can no longer trust my own body

issues.explanation: 'Being naked' is hard to reconcile as a salient trigger for a life-threatening illness trauma unless there was a very specific exposure context; the other items point more toward nightmares/body sensations/illness-related reexperiencing, so this trigger appears poorly matched to the trauma type.

issues.item: Threat: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
issues.explanation: Risk-taking is not well supported by the rest of the profile. The other threat and memory items describe fear, bodily alarm, pain, sensory recall, and dysregulated emotion rather than impulsive or reckless responding, so this item stands out as clinically disconnected.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Mistrust: People can't be trusted
issues.explanation: Global mistrust of other people is a weak fit with a primary trauma of life-threatening illness in the absence of any interpersonal betrayal, assault, or persecution content elsewhere in the profile. The rest of the appraisals are centered on bodily threat and fear of losing control, making this item comparatively incoherent.

vignette: Amir's life was forever altered on a sweltering summer day two years ago when he was rushed to the hospital with excruciating chest pain. The diagnosis - a severe case of pneumonia that had progressed to sepsis - left him fighting for his life. As a hairdresser, Amir was no stranger to high-pressure situations, but nothing could have prepared him for the trauma that awaited him in those sterile hospital corridors. The memory of that fateful day still lingered vividly in Amir's mind. He recalled the antiseptic smell wafting through the air as he lay helplessly on the hospital bed, the beeping of machines echoing in his ears, and the feeling of utter powerlessness that gripped him as the medical team frantically worked to stabilize his condition. Even now, whenever he caught a whiff of disinfectant, Amir was instantly transported back to those harrowing moments. As Amir slowly began to recover from his ordeal, he noticed that certain triggers would set off a chain reaction within him. Looking at photos taken during his hospital stay or undergoing routine medical check-ups would send his body into overdrive, leaving him tense and ready to react to any perceived danger. The aftermath of nightmares, too, left Amir reeling - the residue of fear and anxiety clinging to him like a shroud. What frightened Amir most was the constant threat he perceived within himself. His negative emotions - fear, horror, anger, guilt, and shame - swirled together in a toxic brew that seemed impossible to contain. He felt as though his body was perpetually on high alert, ready to respond to any danger, real or imagined. Even the slightest provocation could trigger a physical reaction, leaving Amir feeling as though he was losing control. Amir's memories of his illness lingered, refusing to be exorcised. The smell of antiseptic would waft up, transporting him back to those hospital corridors, and he'd feel a searing pain in his chest - the same spot where the pneumonia had ravaged his body. Sometimes, Amir couldn't shake off the emotional intensity of that experience even when no clear image or memory presented itself. The aftermath of his trauma had left Amir with a crippling sense of distrust in his own body. He believed it was an enemy, perpetually reacting as if danger lurked around every corner, even when he knew he was safe. The fear that he might be "going crazy" due to his erratic reactions consumed him, eroding what little confidence remained. As the months dragged on, Amir's avoidance behaviors became more entrenched. He began to shy away from social engagements, unable to bear the thought of being around people while feeling so vulnerable. His work as a hairdresser suffered too - the proximity to chemicals and disinfectants proved too much for him to handle. The tension in his body was palpable, causing his hands to shake as he tried to style clients' hair. The final straw came when Amir's best friend, Rachel, staged an intervention, expressing her concern over his increasing isolation and erratic behavior. It was then that Amir realized he needed help - not just for himself but also for the relationships he cherished. He hoped that therapy would provide a safe space to untangle the web of emotions that had entangled him since his illness. As Amir sat in the therapist's office, he couldn't shake off the fear that lingered within him. What if he truly was losing his grip on reality? What if his body continued to betray him at every turn? The uncertainty hung over him like a specter, casting a shadow over his fragile hopes for recovery.
